claims.text: Adding a few atomic percent Pd to equiatomic CoCrFeNi promotes short-range ordering.
Pd-enhanced short-range order creates local resistance to deformation and dislocation slip.
Increased dislocation glide resistance caused by short-range order raises yield strength.
A minor Pd addition produces higher yield strength than an undoped CoCrFeNi baseline.
The proposed baseline CoCrFeNi alloy is a single-phase disordered solid solution.
The proposed baseline CoCrFeNi alloy has high ductility and strength.
Pd-doped material should exhibit lower dislocation velocities than the undoped baseline.
Pd-doped material should exhibit more rugged dislocation-line configurations than the undoped baseline.
The undoped baseline exhibits smoother dislocation glide than the Pd-doped alloy.
The mechanism is expected to apply when dislocation glide is the primary deformation mode.
The mechanism is expected to apply only when Pd-induced ordering does not trigger phase transformations or other significant microstructural changes.
Alloy chemistry, processing history, and testing temperature may affect the magnitude of strengthening and dislocation pinning.
Prior CoCrFeNiPd evidence supports an association among Pd, enhanced short-range ordering, greater glide resistance, and higher yield strength.
The effect of Pd-induced short-range order may vary across different high-entropy-alloy compositions.
Identically tested undoped and Pd-doped samples provide the proposed controlled comparison.
Yield strength, flow stress, dislocation behavior, and short-range order are proposed as measurable experimental variables.
Failure to observe statistically significant strengthening together with evidence of Pd-induced SRO and hindered glide would falsify the proposed mechanism.
